state_definitions.strength: Supported inside this fictional corpus; not a real University finding.
state_definitions.gap: A deliberately constructed evidence-backed inconsistency or missing practice in the fictional corpus.
state_definitions.unknown: The corpus intentionally does not establish the fact; downstream tools must preserve uncertainty.

facts.statement: Planned changes use a fictional request record with acceptance criteria linked to implementation and test evidence.
Regression fixtures for fictional academic rule-table changes are not consistently refreshed with the rule version.
Access-sensitive application changes include a documented security-review prompt in the fictional review workflow.
The collection does not establish whether any ESS-like test data is production-derived or how such data would be handled.
The fictional ESS team uses release windows, a rollback decision record, and post-release service checks for planned releases.
Two fictional post-incident improvement actions have owners but no evidence of effectiveness review after closure.
Two fictional AI-assisted documentation trials use different evaluation notes and cannot be compared directly.
No evidence in the collection establishes generative-AI use in ESS-like production release decisions.
Two fictional external integrations have versioned contract tests tied to their current interface versions.
The fictional RIS architecture overview predates a major integration change and its replacement decision record is absent.
Two fictional nonhuman integration identities have documented purpose but no current accountable owner role in the inventory.
A fictional weekly vulnerability-triage record distinguishes accepted risk, remediation work, duplicates, and unverified closure.
A fictional deployment requires one manual ordering step that exists only in interview testimony, not the runbook.
A fictional overnight batch failure runbook includes escalation, replay controls, and a recorded recovery verification.
A fictional research-description summarization pilot has a frozen evaluation set, expected answers, and repair-effort observations.
The fictional AI pilot has an owner and monitoring notes but no explicit disable or retirement criterion.
Fictional identity-service changes preserve request, review, test, artifact, and deployment identifiers in one trace chain.
Two fictional emergency changes show production restoration but only one has documented follow-up review evidence.
Fictional joiner, mover, and leaver samples link authorization decisions to downstream completion evidence.
Fictional privileged administrative changes require MFA and produce an auditable change record.
The fictional sign-in service has stated availability and latency objectives with alert-to-incident ownership.
The collection contains a written migration rollback procedure but no evidence of a demonstrated stateful-data recovery exercise.
The collection contains no evidence that AI participates in identity authorization or entitlement decisions.
A fictional governance note explicitly prohibits autonomous AI-driven access changes without a human-approved change path.
